5. The integer-bit transfer can be completed conditionally

The missing exponent cannot be replaced by a tensor oracle. But once the requisite finite identities are proved to exist, uniform construction and bit accounting can be supplied.


Certificate format and exact verification

Use a finite integer-normalized bilinear identity
$D(AB)_{ij}
=
\sum_{s=1}^{r}W_{ij,s}
\left(\sum_{\alpha,\beta}U_{s,\alpha\beta}A_{\alpha\beta}\right)
\left(\sum_{\gamma,\eta}V_{s,\gamma\eta}B_{\gamma\eta}\right),
\tag{17}$
for $v\times v$ matrices, with $D>0$ and integer arrays $U,V,W$.

Verify all $v^6$ equations
$\sum_sW_{ij,s}U_{s,\alpha\beta}V_{s,\gamma\eta}
=
D\,\mathbf1_{\{\alpha=i,\ \beta=\gamma,\ \eta=j\}}.
\tag{18}$
This proves the identity for every input. It also proves validity for matrix blocks, because every term retains the order “$A$-entry followed by $B$-entry.”

For a fixed rational $\delta=p/q>0$, seek
$r<v^{2+\delta/2}.
\tag{19}$
The inequality is decidable exactly by
$r^{2q}<v^{4q+p}.$

A modulus that keeps every intermediate bounded

Let the input entries have absolute value below $2^b$. Put
$L=\lceil\log_v n\rceil,\qquad N=v^L,$
and pad to side $N$. Define
$K=2b+\lceil\log_2(2N)\rceil,
\qquad
Q=D\,2^K+1.
\tag{20}$
Then
$\gcd(D,Q)=1,
\qquad
D^{-1}\equiv-2^K\pmod Q.
\tag{21}$
Perform the entire recursive computation over $\mathbb Z/Q\mathbb Z$, using the unnormalized identity. Its depth-$L$ result is
$D^L AB\pmod Q.$
The exponent is $L$, not the total number of nodes, because each level combines child products linearly.

Multiply the final entries by $(-2^K)^L\bmod Q$, computed by binary exponentiation. Since
$|(AB)_{ij}|<n2^{2b}<Q/2,$
centered lifting returns the exact signed integer product.

No prime search, factorization, variable-precision cancellation estimate or rational division inside the recursion is needed. Modular division and reduction are ordinary charged computations.


Time and storage

Let
$B_*=b+\lceil\log_2(2n)\rceil.$
Every residue has
$O_\delta(B_*)$
bits. The fixed coefficient arrays and their reductions are charged as well.

A node of side $t$ uses $O_{v,r}(t^2)$ scalar operations outside its recursive calls. Since a valid identity has $r\ge v^2$, total work is bounded by
$O_{v,r}\bigl((1+L)r^L\bigr),
\qquad
r^L\le r\,n^{\log_v r}.$
